claim: Kim et al. use attack success probability (ASP) as an attacker-side effectiveness metric
quote: the attack model evaluates the success probability of each phase of the CKC framework. ... The attack success probability (𝐴𝑆𝑃 ) can be computed by the Eq. 2:
locator: p. 10 printed (PDF p. 10), Sec. 6.1.3 and 6.3, Eq. 2
issue: Kim's ASP is a product of per-CKC-phase terms; the plain ASP label fits.

claim: Kim et al. is a recent MTD evaluation that describes its attacker by the Cyber Kill Chain or ATT&CK
quote: We generate automated exploits to run Remote Code Execution (RCE), which is one of the MITRE ATT&CK oﬀensive techniques (i.e., T1059) [1]. The automated attack consists of four stages of the CKC
issue: Published 2026 (FGCS 181, 108419). Provenance from-memory, but the claim holds.

claim: Kim et al. scored: 1 in part, 2 none, 3 none, 4 none, 5 in part, 6 none, 7 none, 8 none (Table 3.3)
quote: The automated attack consists of four stages of the CKC and its objective is to compromise a vulnerability (i.e., CVE 2021–41773) of an Apache web server [87]. ... it assumes that creating an outbound connection is attempted in order to evade the detection by a defense system such as a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) or a ﬁrewall. ... This work proposes a single attack scenario and follows sequential steps.
issue: Every mark checked against Kim's own description: multi-stage but one short attempt (1 in part); one objective (2); single scenario (3); no response to a deployment, the attack is disconnected (4); evasion only assumed, no IDS in the testbed (5); no cost, learning or scheme logic modelled (6-8).

claim: Kim et al. use a real testbed, an SDN on physical hardware, to evaluate an MTD combining virtual IP shuffling, software diversity and redundancy
quote: validates the performance and security of our MTD approach in a physical, real testbed, not a simulation or emulation testbed. ... Fig. 5 represents the implementation of vIP shuﬄing, software diversity, and redundancy techniques at edge switches of an SDN network.
locator: p. 2 printed (PDF p. 2), Sec. 2; p. 8 printed (PDF p. 8), Sec. 5.3.1
issue: Kim evaluates five combinations of the three, the full combination among them; 'an MTD that combines' is a fair summary.

claim: The attacker model is an automated script of four stages in a fixed order: scan for web servers, collect service versions, exploit one Apache vulnerability, keep a reverse shell
quote: This work splits the reconnaissance phase into two steps to disclose information about a target. It assumes that an attacker has a lack of network information about a target so it ﬁrst scans the IP addresses of web servers that open the HTTP port 80.
issue: Uncited neighbour leaning on kim2026; the four stages, the Apache CVE and the outbound (reverse) connection are all in Sec. 5.2 and Sec. 4 (p. 7, 'reverse connections').

claim: Each attack is a new run of the script, started at a random time
quote: For security evaluation, the attack workloads follow the Poisson distribution with the attack rate (𝐴𝑇 𝐾𝜆) of 0.2 [#/min.].
issue: Uncited neighbour leaning on kim2026; Poisson arrivals carry 'random time'.

claim: Campaign persistence in part: each attack runs all four stages in one short attempt, and the next starts again with no knowledge of the network
quote: It assumes that an attacker has a lack of network information about a target so it ﬁrst scans the IP addresses of web servers that open the HTTP port 80.
issue: Uncited neighbour; 'one short attempt' follows from the attack being bounded by the 300 s MTD interval (Eq. for T_k, p. 10), a reading rather than Kim's words.

claim: The reverse shell is chosen 'in order to evade the detection by a defense system' (p. 7), but the testbed runs no IDS, so the evasion is assumed
quote: After the attacker succeeds to connect to a victim, it assumes that creating an outbound connection is attempted in order to evade the detection by a defense system such as a network intrusion detection system (NIDS) or a ﬁrewall. ... It comprises SDN-enabled switches, web servers, a legitimate client, and an attacker.
locator: p. 7 printed (PDF p. 7), Sec. 5.2 and Sec. 5.1
issue: Quote and pinpoint exact; 'no IDS' is inferred from the testbed's listed components (Sec. 5.1, Sec. 6.1), which name none. Kim's own 'it assumes' carries 'assumed'.

claim: No objective-specific behaviour: after the foothold it keeps its shell and installs tools, with one objective; none exfiltrates or impedes
quote: The attacker can install tools or crafted code in a hidden directory in order to avoid detection by the target’s defense solutions.
issue: Uncited neighbour; one objective per p. 9: 'The objective of the attacker is to obtain a shell connection'.

claim: The attacker 'can determine the remaining available time' before the next deployment (p. 10), so it predicts which mechanism deploys next and when, but no technique leverages it
quote: At each CKC phase (𝑘), attackers can determine the remaining available time (𝑇𝑘) after successfully completing the preceding step. This value can be computed by:
locator: p. 10 printed (PDF p. 10), Sec. 6.1.3, after Eq. 2
issue: Quote and pinpoint exact, but in Kim the sentence introduces T_k, a term of the ASP equation (Eq. 2); nothing in the attack model (Sec. 5.2) has the script compute or use it. 'So it predicts' over-credits; the 'none' mark holds either way.
fix_text: 'so it predicts which mechanism deploys next and when' -> 'so it could predict which mechanism deploys next and when'

claim: No choice of attack strategy: every attack follows one attack scenario in the same four stages
quote: This work proposes a single attack scenario and follows sequential steps.

claim: No adaptivity: the script does not observe the MTD, and an attack a deployment disrupts fails
quote: this study assumes that the connection between an attacker and a target is disconnected during either 𝑇𝐷𝐸𝐼 or 𝑇𝐶2𝐴.
issue: Uncited neighbour; 'does not observe the MTD' sits uneasily beside U0290's 'can determine the remaining available time'. The reconnaissance repeat (up to 5 scans, p. 9) is a fixed retry, not a response to a deployment.

claim: Of the three, only Kim et al.'s has detection avoidance, in part, and none has objective-specific behaviour, cost-benefit reasoning, learning or deployment-strategy awareness
quote: it assumes that creating an outbound connection is attempted in order to evade the detection by a defense system
issue: Uncited summary naming Kim; covered by the Table 3.3 row (U0263) and U0288. Kim's share only checked here.

claim: Kim et al.'s attacker model has none of the eight properties in full
quote: This work proposes a single attack scenario and follows sequential steps.
issue: Uncited summary naming Kim; covered by U0263. Kim's share only checked here.
